subject: Performance qualification: traffic profile, streaming behavior, and p95/p99 asks
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stratusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: traffic profile & streaming behavior (p95/p99 targets)

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of concrete asks so our engineering team can size the hosted POC and map SLOs against your current baseline.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary objective: improve user-perceived latency for inference-driven features (search re-rank + chat snippets).
- Current provider: intermittent p95/p99 spikes during peak; you mentioned some sessions hit p99 ~700ms at peak load.
- Streaming: ~20–30% of requests use streaming (partial tokens to client UI), important for UX.

Concrete asks from Redwood to run an apples-to-apples qualification:
1) Traffic profile CSV (attached sample schema) with: request timestamp, model variant, average token length, payload size (KB), streaming:boolean, and an anonymized session id.
2) Typical and peak concurrency: please confirm sustained RPS and peak concurrent in-flight requests.
3) Target SLOs you care about (p95 and p99). If you don’t have firm numbers, tell us the target bands (e.g., p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms).
4) Any payload/encoding constraints (gzip, chunked streaming).

What we’ll do with that data
- Run a 2-week hosted POC replay on our Redwood hosted API using your traffic mix (synthetic replay).
- Measure end-to-end p95/p99 with and without streaming enabled, and test alternate batch/kv-cache configs.
- Provide a short decision matrix showing expected cost per 1M tokens and recommended config to meet SLOs.

Proposed timeline
- You share traffic CSV and any recent latency report by EOD Mon (2027-04-12).
- We provision the POC and share baseline results within 7 business days of receiving data.

Attachments: I attached a sample traffic_profile CSV (naomi_traffic_profile_v1.csv) — follow that schema to make ingest straightforward.

Next steps
- If you can confirm the CSV and your rough p95/p99 targets, we’ll queue this for Ben and our infra team to schedule the replay.

Thanks — NaomI

--
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stratusai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@stratusai.com>, StratusAI SRE <sre@stratusai.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: traffic profile & streaming behavior (p95/p99 targets)

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clarity. Attaching our latest latency report for the last 30 days (current_provider_latency_report.pdf). Quick answers inline.

- Sustained RPS: ~420 req/s across our primary region during business hours.
- Peak bursts: up to ~1.1k req/s for short windows (1–3 minutes) during batch sync jobs.
- Concurrency (in-flight requests): typical 120–160, peak observed 220.
- Payloads: average 140 tokens (approx 6–8KB JSON payloads); 95th token length ~320 tokens.
- Streaming: ~26% of total requests are streaming; clients open HTTP/2 streams and render partial tokens as they arrive.
- Current provider numbers (baseline): p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 720ms (we care about tail at p99 more than p95, but both matter).

Target SLOs we want to validate are:
- p95 <= 260 ms end-to-end (client-facing)
- p99 <= 550 ms end-to-end

We can provide an anonymized traffic CSV by EOD today. Two notes:
1) We do a small amount of batched requests (up to 4 prompts in one call) — traffic CSV will indicate batch_size.
2) Some clients set 'max_tokens' aggressively; we’ll flag those rows so you can run separate buckets.

We’re happy to run the POC on Redwood hosted. What do you need from us besides the CSV and the baseline report? Also, any minimum RW account permissions to spin up the harness?

— Alex

On Fri, Apr 10, 2027 at 15:12 Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks again for the call this morning... (original message quoted for context)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stratusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: traffic profile & streaming behavior (p95/p99 targets)

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick data. A few clarifications before we kick the replay off:

1) Sampling approach
- If you can send a full-enough slice with at least two full business days of representative traffic (CSV preferred), we’ll run an exact-replay test. If full data is sensitive, a stratified sample that preserves session-level concurrency patterns is fine.

2) Streaming reproduction details
- We reproduce streaming by keeping the connection open and returning partial chunks at the same token cadence you provide. Please indicate for streaming rows: average chunk size (tokens) and average inter-chunk delay.

3) Measurement boundary
- Our measurements will be end-to-end from Redwood ingress to Redwood egress to client-facing delivery time. We’ll also provide breakdowns: network + server processing + serialization.

4) Pass/fail criteria suggestion (we can adapt to yours)
- Baseline pass: hosted POC shows p95 within 1.2x of your target and p99 within 1.4x, plus consistent CPU/GPU utilization below thresholds.
- Stretch pass: p95 <= 260ms and p99 <= 550ms across sustained workload.

What we need from you now
- CSV (or access to SRE to pull an anonymized slice) + confirmation on streaming chunk cadence and batch mix.
- A sandbox API key (or permission to create an agent in your staging workspace) so we can send traffic to the Redwood-hosted endpoint you want validated.

I’ll ask Ben to draft the POC schedule and test matrix. Once we have the CSV and a sandbox key, we’ll provision and run the baseline within 72 hours.

Thanks — Naomi

> On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 09:03 Alex Turner <alex.turner@stratusai.com> wrote:
> > Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clarity...
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stratusai.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: traffic profile & streaming behavior (p95/p99 targets)

Alex — Ben here (Infra & SE). Quick operational plan and timeline so you have a clear view of what we’ll run.

High-level POC plan
- Day 0: Receive CSV + sandbox key from StratusAI. Confirm streaming cadence fields and any special headers.
- Day 1: Small dry-run (10k requests) to validate replay tooling and schema ingestion.
- Day 2–3: Baseline replay at your sustained RPS (420 req/s) for 4 hours. Collect p50/p95/p99 and resource traces.
- Day 4: Peak burst simulation (1.1k req/s) in short windows to validate queuing/backpressure and fallback policies.
- Day 5: Streaming-focused test (replicate your 26% streaming mix) and measure chunk-latency vs full-response-latency.
- Day 6–7: Run variations (small batch sizes, quantized model variant) and produce the report.

Deliverables
- Raw latency histograms and a breakdown CSV.
- Config recommendation (batching, kv-cache TTLs, concurrency limits) and cost estimate.
- A short exec one-pager mapping hosted vs your incumbent for p95/p99 and cost.

Questions/asks for you
- Please provide the CSV (anonymized) and a sandbox API key by EOD Wed (2027-04-14). If you need an NDA/POC agreement, flag that and we’ll route to legal.
- Are there any hard throttles or client-side timeouts we should be aware of (e.g., client 700 ms timeout)? If so, share the values so we can model graceful degradation.

Proposed meeting: 2027-04-15 10:00 PT to review baseline output and next steps. I’ll send a calendar invite once we have the data.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
